svg.title: PipelineProof — full 25-scenario attack and architecture map
svg.desc: All 25 documented attack scenarios, exact code locations, fixed controls, local fixture boundaries, separate real Kubernetes lab, security gates and evidence storage.
svg.text: Attack paths, runtime boundaries and lab structure
Vulnerable effect → fixed retest → legitimate result
Temporary working directories; synthetic data only
Manual kind and live-security-tool jobs are separate
The groups below locate code and fixtures; they are not 24 deployed network services.
Docker: non-root · read-only root · no Docker socket
Loopback mocks work inside the network-disabled container.
Synthetic build steps and a loopback JSON package index.

g.title: 25: fail-open-error-handling — CWE-636
g.text: Fix: Explicit allow; deny on error

svg.text: Module-local state; optional labs/web.py on 127.0.0.1:8081 (fixed by default).
In-memory SQLite + temporary files; high-risk proofs are CLI-only.
HTTP vulnerable mode requires both explicit flags:
HTTP adapter uses synthetic login; the password-storage lab is separate.
HMAC is a shared-key MAC; local JSONL is not a deployed SIEM.
Both: 127.0.0.1, allocated ports; no external destinations or redirects.
12 uses a separate loopback JSON package index; no public package installs.

g.title: 05: excessive-permissions — real Kubernetes API
g.text: Vulnerable: wildcard Role permits fake Secret read
Fixed: Secret read forbidden; Deployment patch allowed
Real API requests via CI-identity impersonation; requires kind + Docker.
Not started by native setup or make lab. No cloud accounts involved.

svg.text: 24 local proofs + fresh scenario 05 evidence = full audit
Each proof: exploit observed · fixed attack blocked
Positive checks preserve the intended legitimate behavior.

Fixed-code findings block; teaching findings are separate.
Release policy blocks HIGH / CRITICAL image findings.
Outputs: JSON · SARIF where supported · SBOM · HTML
kind configuration, deployment and RBAC manifests
